svg.title: The life of one interrupt
svg.desc: Top: with IRQs masked, a level line stays pending until the CPU unmasks, an edge with no latch is lost, and a latched edge waits in its latch. Bottom: the four GIC states of INTID 33. Raising the line makes it pending; reading the IAR makes it active, or active and pending while a level line is still high; lowering the line removes the pending half; writing the EOI makes it inactive, or pending again if a level line is still high, which is an interrupt storm.

g.text: level line: pending ... still pending ... handler runs
edge, no latch: pulse, gone ... nothing pending ... nothing happens
edge, latched: latch set ... still pending ... handler runs
An edge: the IAR clears pending even with the line high, so the EOI ends it.
